chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, all together from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from one of our companions, who said:

When Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) arrived in Al-Hira, he rode his animal and went to Al-Khwarraq. So he descended and took shade in the shadow of his animal, and with him was a black slave of his. He saw a man from the people of Kufa who had bought a palm tree. He said to the slave, 'Who is this?' He said to him, 'This is Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him)'.

So he brought a large platter and placed it in front of him. He said to the man, 'What is this?' He said, 'This is Al-Barniy'. He said, 'Therein is a healing'. And he looked at Al-Sabiri, so he said, 'What is this?' He said, 'Al-Sabiri'. He said, 'This with us is Al-Bayd'. And he said for Al-Mushan, 'What is this?' So the man said, 'Al-Mushan'. He said (peace be upon him), 'This with us is Umm Jirzan'. And he looked at Al-Sarfan, so he said, 'What is this?' So the man said, 'Al-Sarfan'. He said, 'With us it is Al-Ajwa and therein is a healing'.

key_terms.أُمُّ جِرْذَانَ: Umm Jirzan, a specific name for a date variety in the terminology of the Ahl al-Bayt.
key_terms.الْبِيض: Al-Bayd, meaning 'the white ones', a local name for a date variety.
key_terms.الْحِيرَة: Al-Hira, a city in Iraq near Kufa.
key_terms.الْخَوَرْنَق: Al-Khwarraq, a specific location or area in Al-Hira.
key_terms.الْعَجْوَةُ: Al-Ajwa, a highly regarded variety of dates known for its healing properties.

ai.seo_question: What are the different names for dates mentioned in Shia hadith and their spiritual or physical benefits?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Imam’s role as the authoritative interpreter of local customs, correcting Kufan dialects to align with the terminology of the Ahl al-Bayt. It underscores the spiritual and physical healing (*shifa*) inherent in specific date varieties like Al-Barniy and Al-Ajwa, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the Imam’s comprehensive knowledge of both religious and worldly matters. The narrative serves as a practical guide for distinguishing authentic traditions from regional variations in daily life.
